story.thread: Hidden data in AI work files
story.thread_subtitle: what raw technical sessions may carry outside the readable chat
story.headline: AI work logs can carry secrets you cannot see. Here’s what to share instead
story.the_story: A new security preprint found real passwords, access keys and personal information inside publicly shared technical AI-session files, including some material that was absent from the visible conversation. The authors say the affected providers patched the specific attacks after disclosure.
story.laidies_read: This is not evidence that every private consumer chat suddenly became public. It is evidence that a cleaned chat window and a safe raw technical session are different things: opaque carry-over data can travel inside the session even when the visible answer looks clean.
story.what_this_means: Share the checked result you intend people to read, not the whole technical session that made it. Teams that publish raw logs should build a fresh release file from approved fields, strip opaque reasoning or signature fields and rotate any credential that may already have been exposed.
story.cocktail_party: Researchers found that some public AI work logs carried passwords and access keys outside the visible chat. The companies patched the specific attacks, but a cleaned transcript still is not the same as a safe raw log.
story.watch_fors: A corrected paper, provider statement, independent reproduction or material change to reasoning and signature-field handling.
story.closing_note: Share the result you chose—not the entire technical session that made it.
story.class_notes: The durable distinction is between an approved output and the complete production record that created it; a visible redaction does not inventory the latter.
